section_1.title: The Context Problem: Why Words Need Neighbors
section_1.content: Introduce the core challenge in Natural Language Processing: polysemy and context. Explain that a word's meaning is fluid and depends entirely on the words surrounding it. This section sets the stage for why 'attention' is necessary for computers to understand nuances.
section_1.example: Show two sentences: 'The crane flew over the construction site' vs 'The crane lifted the heavy beam.' An animation highlights the word 'crane' and draws lines to 'flew' in the first and 'heavy beam' in the second to show shifting meaning.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Coordinate System of Language
section_2.content: Briefly explain Vector Embeddings. Words are converted into lists of numbers (vectors) representing coordinates in a high-dimensional space. Words with similar meanings are physically closer in this space. This is the mathematical foundation needed to perform calculations.
section_2.example: A 3D graph showing 'King' and 'Queen' close together, while 'Apple' is far away in another cluster. Visualizing the subtraction: King - Man + Woman = Queen.

section_3.title: The Library Analogy: Query, Key, and Value
section_3.content: Introduce the three functional components of the Attention mechanism: Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V). Explain the mechanism as a database search where the 'Query' is what you are looking for, 'Key' is the label on the shelf, and 'Value' is the information inside.
section_3.example: A character named 'Detective Query' enters a library. He holds a note (The Word). The library shelves have labels (Keys). He compares his note to every label to see which one matches (Similarity Score). Once matched, he takes the book content (Value) from the shelf.

section_4.title: The Math of Focus: Dot Products and Softmax
section_4.content: Visualize the mathematical process of calculating 'Attention Scores.' Use the Dot Product to measure the alignment (similarity) between Q and K. Apply the Softmax function to turn these scores into percentages (weights) that sum to 100%.
section_4.example: A graphic showing the word 'Eating' (Query) interacting with 'Robot' (Key 1) and 'Pizza' (Key 2). The dot product produces a high score for 'Pizza'. Softmax turns this into: Pizza (90% focus), Robot (10% focus).

section_5.title: Multi-Head Attention: Many Perspectives at Once
section_5.content: Explain that Transformers don't just look at a sentence once; they look at it through 'Multi-Head Attention.' Each 'head' focuses on different relationships like grammar, tense, or sentiment simultaneously.
section_5.example: An owl with multiple sets of eyes. One set of eyes looks for 'Who did what?' (Subject-Verb), another set looks for 'Where did it happen?' (Location), and a third looks for 'How does it feel?' (Sentiment).

section_6.title: The Result: Contextualized Understanding
section_6.content: Summarize how the weighted 'Values' are summed to create a new, context-aware vector for the word. This 'updated' word now carries the history of its neighbors, allowing Large Language Models like GPT to generate coherent text.
section_6.example: The original gray vector for 'Bank' absorbs colors from nearby words 'River' and 'Water.' The resulting vector glows blue, representing a 'River Bank' rather than a 'Financial Bank.' This enables the model to predict the next word: 'Flowing'.

section_3.content: Introduce the three functional components of the Attention mechanism: Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V). Explain the mechanism as a database search where the 'Query' is what you are looking for, 'Key' is the label on the shelf, and 'Value' is the information inside.
section_3.example: A character named 'Detective Query' enters a library. He holds a note (The Word). The library shelves have labels (Keys). He compares his note to every label to see which one matches (Similarity Score). Once matched, he takes the book content (Value) from the shelf.

section_4.title: The Math of Focus: Dot Products and Softmax
section_4.content: Visualize the mathematical process of calculating 'Attention Scores.' Use the Dot Product to measure the alignment (similarity) between Q and K. Apply the Softmax function to turn these scores into percentages (weights) that sum to 100%.
section_4.example: A graphic showing the word 'Eating' (Query) interacting with 'Robot' (Key 1) and 'Pizza' (Key 2). The dot product produces a high score for 'Pizza'. Softmax turns this into: Pizza (90% focus), Robot (10% focus).

section_5.title: Multi-Head Attention: Many Perspectives at Once
section_5.content: Explain that Transformers don't just look at a sentence once; they look at it through 'Multi-Head Attention.' Each 'head' focuses on different relationships like grammar, tense, or sentiment simultaneously.
section_5.example: An owl with multiple sets of eyes. One set of eyes looks for 'Who did what?' (Subject-Verb), another set looks for 'Where did it happen?' (Location), and a third looks for 'How does it feel?' (Sentiment).

section_6.title: The Result: Contextualized Understanding
section_6.content: Summarize how the weighted 'Values' are summed to create a new, context-aware vector for the word. This 'updated' word now carries the history of its neighbors, allowing Large Language Models like GPT to generate coherent text.
section_6.example: The original gray vector for 'Bank' absorbs colors from nearby words 'River' and 'Water.' The resulting vector glows blue, representing a 'River Bank' rather than a 'Financial Bank.' This enables the model to predict the next word: 'Flowing'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Math of Focus: Dot Products and Softmax", [
            "- Dot products measure alignment between Queries and Keys.",
            "- Softmax converts these scores into percentage weights.",
            "- Higher weights signal stronger focus on specific words.",
            "- The sum of all weights equals 100 percent.",
            "- This math directs the model's spotlight precisely."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Q (Eating, #00FFFF)
        q_label = Text("Q: 'Eating'", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, "C2")
        
        # K1 (Robot, #FF6347) and K2 (Pizza, #FF6347)
        k1_label = Text("K1: 'Robot'", font_size=24, color="#FF6347")
        k2_label = Text("K2: 'Pizza'", font_size=24, color="#FF6347")
        self.place_at_grid(k1_label, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(k2_label, "D5")

        # Visualizing vectors/connections
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["B5"], buff=0.4, color=WHITE)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["D5"], buff=0.4, color=WHITE)

        self.play(FadeIn(q_label), FadeIn(k1_label), FadeIn(k2_label))
        self.play(Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2))

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show the Dot Product calculation Q · K1 and Q · K2
        dot1 = MathTex("Q \\cdot K_1 = 0.1", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        dot2 = MathTex("Q \\cdot K_2 = 0.9", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot1, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(dot2, "D4")

        self.play(Write(dot1), Write(dot2))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Pizza result glowing brighter
        self.play(Indicate(dot2, color=YELLOW, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Transition to Softmax bar chart
        # Remove intermediate elements
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrow1), FadeOut(arrow2), 
            FadeOut(dot1), FadeOut(dot2),
            q_label.animate.scale(0.7).move_to(self.grid["A2"])
        )

        # Softmax layer represented by a bar chart
        bar_robot = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#FF6347", stroke_width=2)
        bar_pizza = Rectangle(height=3.6, width=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        # Labels for bars
        label_robot = Text("Robot", font_size=20)
        label_pizza = Text("Pizza", font_size=20)

        # Group and position
        chart_bars = VGroup(bar_robot, bar_pizza).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(chart_bars, "C4", "F6")
        
        label_robot.next_to(bar_robot, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        label_pizza.next_to(bar_pizza, DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # Higher weights signal stronger focus
        self.play(Create(chart_bars), FadeIn(label_robot), FadeIn(label_pizza))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Scale bars to show 90% and 10% focus weights (already drawn at relative heights)
        weight_robot = Text("10%", font_size=24).next_to(bar_robot, UP, buff=0.1)
        weight_pizza = Text("90%", font_size=24).next_to(bar_pizza, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        sum_check = MathTex("10\\% + 90\\% = 100\\%", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_check, "B4")

        self.play(FadeIn(weight_robot), FadeIn(weight_pizza))
        self.play(Write(sum_check))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Highlight the resulting focus on 'Pizza' with a glowing border (#FFFF00)
        focus_border = SurroundingRectangle(bar_pizza, color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(focus_border))
        self.play(focus_border.animate.set_stroke(width=8))

            "Similarity scores determine how much information to take.",

        lines = [

            "Similar meanings sit closer in high-dimensional space.",
            "Mathematical distances reveal relationships between words."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        color_king = "#FFD700"
        color_queen = "#FF69B4"
        color_man = "#1E90FF"
        color_woman = "#EE82EE"
        color_apple = "#FF4500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Coordinate System (Axes)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_C},
            tips=True
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(axes))

        p_king = axes.c2p(1, 4)
        p_queen = axes.c2p(4, 4)
        p_man = axes.c2p(1, 1)
        p_woman = axes.c2p(4, 1)
        p_apple = axes.c2p(4.5, 2.5)

        dot_king = Dot(p_king, color=color_king)
        dot_queen = Dot(p_queen, color=color_queen)
        dot_man = Dot(p_man, color=color_man)
        dot_woman = Dot(p_woman, color=color_woman)
        dot_apple = Dot(p_apple, color=color_apple)

        label_king = MathTex(r"\text{King}", color=color_king, font_size=20).next_to(dot_king, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_queen = MathTex(r"\text{Queen}", color=color_queen, font_size=20).next_to(dot_queen, UP, buff=0.1)

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

section_1.title: The Context Problem: Why Words Need Neighbors
section_1.content: Introduce the core challenge in Natural Language Processing: polysemy and context. Explain that a word's meaning is fluid and depends entirely on the words surrounding it. This section sets the stage for why 'attention' is necessary for computers to understand nuances.
section_1.example: Show two sentences: 'The crane flew over the construction site' vs 'The crane lifted the heavy beam.' An animation highlights the word 'crane' and draws lines to 'flew' in the first and 'heavy beam' in the second to show shifting meaning.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Coordinate System of Language
section_2.content: Briefly explain Vector Embeddings. Words are converted into lists of numbers (vectors) representing coordinates in a high-dimensional space. Words with similar meanings are physically closer in this space. This is the mathematical foundation needed to perform calculations.
section_2.example: A 3D graph showing 'King' and 'Queen' close together, while 'Apple' is far away in another cluster. Visualizing the subtraction: King - Man + Woman = Queen.

section_3.title: The Library Analogy: Query, Key, and Value
section_3.content: Introduce the three functional components of the Attention mechanism: Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V). Explain the mechanism as a database search where the 'Query' is what you are looking for, 'Key' is the label on the shelf, and 'Value' is the information inside.
section_3.example: A character named 'Detective Query' enters a library. He holds a note (The Word). The library shelves have labels (Keys). He compares his note to every label to see which one matches (Similarity Score). Once matched, he takes the book content (Value) from the shelf.

section_4.title: The Math of Focus: Dot Products and Softmax
section_4.content: Visualize the mathematical process of calculating 'Attention Scores.' Use the Dot Product to measure the alignment (similarity) between Q and K. Apply the Softmax function to turn these scores into percentages (weights) that sum to 100%.
section_4.example: A graphic showing the word 'Eating' (Query) interacting with 'Robot' (Key 1) and 'Pizza' (Key 2). The dot product produces a high score for 'Pizza'. Softmax turns this into: Pizza (90% focus), Robot (10% focus).

section_5.title: Multi-Head Attention: Many Perspectives at Once
section_5.content: Explain that Transformers don't just look at a sentence once; they look at it through 'Multi-Head Attention.' Each 'head' focuses on different relationships like grammar, tense, or sentiment simultaneously.
section_5.example: An owl with multiple sets of eyes. One set of eyes looks for 'Who did what?' (Subject-Verb), another set looks for 'Where did it happen?' (Location), and a third looks for 'How does it feel?' (Sentiment).

section_6.title: The Result: Contextualized Understanding
section_6.content: Summarize how the weighted 'Values' are summed to create a new, context-aware vector for the word. This 'updated' word now carries the history of its neighbors, allowing Large Language Models like GPT to generate coherent text.
section_6.example: The original gray vector for 'Bank' absorbs colors from nearby words 'River' and 'Water.' The resulting vector glows blue, representing a 'River Bank' rather than a 'Financial Bank.' This enables the model to predict the next word: 'Flowing'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Context Problem: Why Words Need Neighbors",
            [
                "Words often have multiple meanings.",
                "Context defines which meaning is correct.",
                "Attention helps models focus on relevant neighbors."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        s1_words_list = ["The", "crane", "flew", "over", "the", "construction", "site"]
        s1 = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=24, color="#ADD8E6") for w in s1_words_list]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(s1, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(s1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        s2_words_list = ["The", "crane", "lifted", "the", "heavy", "beam"]
        s2 = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=24, color="#90EE90") for w in s2_words_list]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(s2, "E1", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(s2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        # Highlight 'crane' (index 1 in both sentences)
        crane1 = s1[1]
        crane2 = s2[1]
        
        # Targets for arrows
        flew = s1[2]
        heavy_beam = VGroup(s2[4], s2[5]) # 'heavy' and 'beam'

        arrow1 = Arrow(crane1.get_bottom(), flew.get_top(), color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        arrow2 = Arrow(crane2.get_top(), heavy_beam.get_bottom(), color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            crane1.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            crane2.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            Create(arrow1),
            Create(arrow2)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup color for final state
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: The Coordinate System of Language"
        lines = [
            "Computers represent words as numerical vectors.",
            "Similar meanings sit closer in high-dimensional space.",
            "Mathematical distances reveal relationships between words."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        color_king = "#FFD700"
        color_queen = "#FF69B4"
        color_man = "#1E90FF"
        color_woman = "#EE82EE"
        color_apple = "#FF4500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Coordinate System (Axes)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_C},
            tips=True
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(axes))

        # Initial word positions (Spread out)
        p_king = axes.c2p(1, 4)
        p_queen = axes.c2p(4, 4)
        p_man = axes.c2p(1, 1)
        p_woman = axes.c2p(4, 1)
        p_apple = axes.c2p(4.5, 2.5)

        dot_king = Dot(p_king, color=color_king)
        dot_queen = Dot(p_queen, color=color_queen)
        dot_man = Dot(p_man, color=color_man)
        dot_woman = Dot(p_woman, color=color_woman)
        dot_apple = Dot(p_apple, color=color_apple)

        label_king = MathTex(r"\text{King}", color=color_king, font_size=20).next_to(dot_king, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_queen = MathTex(r"\text{Queen}", color=color_queen, font_size=20).next_to(dot_queen, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_man = MathTex(r"\text{Man}", color=color_man, font_size=20).next_to(dot_man, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_woman = MathTex(r"\text{Woman}", color=color_woman, font_size=20).next_to(dot_woman, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_apple = MathTex(r"\text{Apple}", color=color_apple, font_size=20).next_to(dot_apple, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        dots = VGroup(dot_king, dot_queen, dot_man, dot_woman, dot_apple)
        labels = VGroup(label_king, label_queen, label_man, label_woman, label_apple)

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[Create(d) for d in dots],
                *[Write(l) for l in labels],
                lag_ratio=0.2
            )
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Clustered positions
        c_king = axes.c2p(1, 2)
        c_man = axes.c2p(1, 1.2)
        c_queen = axes.c2p(1.8, 2)
        c_woman = axes.c2p(1.8, 1.2)
        c_apple = axes.c2p(4.5, 2.5)

        self.play(
            dot_king.animate.move_to(c_king),
            label_king.animate.next_to(c_king, UP, buff=0.1),
            dot_man.animate.move_to(c_man),
            label_man.animate.next_to(c_man, DOWN, buff=0.1),
            dot_queen.animate.move_to(c_queen),
            label_queen.animate.next_to(c_queen, UP, buff=0.1),
            dot_woman.animate.move_to(c_woman),
            label_woman.animate.next_to(c_woman, DOWN, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Vector Equation
        equation = MathTex(
            r"\vec{v}_{\text{King}}", "-", r"\vec{v}_{\text{Man}}", "+", r"\vec{v}_{\text{Woman}}", "=", r"\vec{v}_{\text{Queen}}",
            font_size=28
        )
        equation[0].set_color(color_king)
        equation[2].set_color(color_man)
        equation[4].set_color(color_woman)
        equation[6].set_color(color_queen)

        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(equation))

        # Show the relationship with arrows
        v_man = Arrow(axes.c2p(0,0), dot_man.get_center(), buff=0, color=color_man, stroke_width=2)
        v_king = Arrow(axes.c2p(0,0), dot_king.get_center(), buff=0, color=color_king, stroke_width=2)
        
        v_diff = Arrow(dot_man.get_center(), dot_king.get_center(), buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(v_man), Create(v_king))
        self.play(Create(v_diff))
        
        target_queen_pos = dot_woman.get_center() + (dot_king.get_center() - dot_man.get_center())
        v_result = Arrow(dot_woman.get_center(), target_queen_pos, buff=0, color=color_queen, stroke_width=3)
        
        self.play(
            v_diff.animate.move_to(dot_woman.get_center() + (dot_king.get_center() - dot_man.get_center())/2),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(Create(v_result))
        
        self.wait(3)

        )
        
        keys = VGroup()

        # Animate "opening"
        self.play(
            keys[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_V).scale(1.1),
            FadeIn(value_group, shift=DOWN)
        )
        
        # Connect Query to Value through Key
        connection = Arrow(query_group.get_bottom(), keys[1].get_top(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(connection))
        
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Math of Focus: Dot Products and Softmax", [
            "- Dot products measure alignment between Queries and Keys.",
            "- Softmax converts these scores into percentage weights.",
            "- Higher weights signal stronger focus on specific words.",
            "- The sum of all weights equals 100 percent.",
            "- This math directs the model's spotlight precisely."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Q (Eating, #00FFFF)
        q_label = Text("Q: 'Eating'", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, "C2")
        
        # K1 (Robot, #FF6347) and K2 (Pizza, #FF6347)
        k1_label = Text("K1: 'Robot'", font_size=24, color="#FF6347")
        k2_label = Text("K2: 'Pizza'", font_size=24, color="#FF6347")
        self.place_at_grid(k1_label, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(k2_label, "D5")

        # Visualizing vectors/connections
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["B5"], buff=0.4, color=WHITE)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["D5"], buff=0.4, color=WHITE)

        self.play(FadeIn(q_label), FadeIn(k1_label), FadeIn(k2_label))
        self.play(Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show the Dot Product calculation Q · K1 and Q · K2
        dot1 = MathTex("Q \\cdot K_1 = 0.1", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        dot2 = MathTex("Q \\cdot K_2 = 0.9", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot1, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(dot2, "D4")

        self.play(Write(dot1), Write(dot2))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Pizza result glowing brighter
        self.play(Indicate(dot2, color=YELLOW, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Transition to Softmax bar chart
        # Remove intermediate elements
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrow1), FadeOut(arrow2), 
            FadeOut(dot1), FadeOut(dot2),
            q_label.animate.scale(0.7).move_to(self.grid["A2"])
        )

        # Softmax layer represented by a bar chart
        bar_robot = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#FF6347", stroke_width=2)
        bar_pizza = Rectangle(height=3.6, width=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        # Labels for bars
        label_robot = Text("Robot", font_size=20)
        label_pizza = Text("Pizza", font_size=20)

        # Group and position
        chart_bars = VGroup(bar_robot, bar_pizza).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(chart_bars, "C4", "F6")
        
        label_robot.next_to(bar_robot, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        label_pizza.next_to(bar_pizza, DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # Higher weights signal stronger focus
        self.play(Create(chart_bars), FadeIn(label_robot), FadeIn(label_pizza))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Scale bars to show 90% and 10% focus weights (already drawn at relative heights)
        weight_robot = Text("10%", font_size=24).next_to(bar_robot, UP, buff=0.1)
        weight_pizza = Text("90%", font_size=24).next_to(bar_pizza, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        sum_check = MathTex("10\\% + 90\\% = 100\\%", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_check, "B4")

        self.play(FadeIn(weight_robot), FadeIn(weight_pizza))
        self.play(Write(sum_check))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Highlight the resulting focus on 'Pizza' with a glowing border (#FFFF00)
        focus_border = SurroundingRectangle(bar_pizza, color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(focus_border))
        self.play(focus_border.animate.set_stroke(width=8))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup / color reset
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        title = "The Result: Contextualized Understanding"
        lines = [
            "Weighted values combine into a new, context-aware vector.",
            "This vector captures the word's current meaning perfectly.",
            "Contextual understanding allows for more human-like AI.",
            "Models can now predict the next logical word.",
            "This is the secret behind powerful language models."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        NEUTRAL_GRAY = "#808080"
        CONTEXT_BLUE = "#1E90FF"
        HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the word 'Bank' represented as a neutral gray vector
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)
        
        bank_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.2, color=NEUTRAL_GRAY, buff=0)
        bank_label = Text("Bank", font_size=24, color=NEUTRAL_GRAY).next_to(bank_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        bank_group = VGroup(bank_arrow, bank_label)
        self.place_in_area(bank_group, "C3", "D4")
        
        self.play(Create(bank_arrow), Write(bank_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display context words 'River' and 'Water' as blue-colored vectors drifting toward 'Bank'
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)

        river_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.8, color=CONTEXT_BLUE, buff=0)
        river_label = Text("River", font_size=20, color=CONTEXT_BLUE).next_to(river_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.place_at_grid(river_group, "B2")

        water_label = Text("Water", font_size=20, color=CONTEXT_BLUE).next_to(water_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.place_at_grid(water_group, "E5")

        self.play(FadeIn(river_group), FadeIn(water_group))
        
        # Drifting animation toward the center (Bank)
        self.play(
            river_group.animate.move_to(bank_group.get_center() + LEFT*0.5 + UP*0.5).set_opacity(0.3),
            water_group.animate.move_to(bank_group.get_center() + RIGHT*0.5 + DOWN*0.5).set_opacity(0.3),

        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)

        self.play(
            bank_arrow.animate.set_color(CONTEXT_BLUE),
            bank_label.animate.set_color(CONTEXT_BLUE),
            FadeOut(river_group),
            FadeOut(water_group),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)

        self.place_at_grid(prediction_group, "F4")

        self.play(Create(prediction_box), Write(prediction_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final emphasis
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)
        
        glow = bank_arrow.copy().set_stroke(width=10).set_color(CONTEXT_BLUE).set_opacity(0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow), bank_group.animate.scale(1.1))
        self.play(FadeOut(glow))
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset colors for end of scene
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

outline.content: Summarize how the weighted 'Values' are summed to create a new, context-aware vector for the word. This 'updated' word now carries the history of its neighbors, allowing Large Language Models like GPT to generate coherent text.
outline.example: The original gray vector for 'Bank' absorbs colors from nearby words 'River' and 'Water.' The resulting vector glows blue, representing a 'River Bank' rather than a 'Financial Bank.' This enables the model to predict the next word: 'Flowing'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Result: Contextualized Understanding"
        lines = [
            "Weighted values combine into a new, context-aware vector.",
            "This vector captures the word's current meaning perfectly.",
            "Contextual understanding allows for more human-like AI.",
            "Models can now predict the next logical word.",
            "This is the secret behind powerful language models."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        NEUTRAL_GRAY = "#808080"
        CONTEXT_BLUE = "#1E90FF"
        HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the word 'Bank' represented as a neutral gray vector
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)
        
        bank_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.2, color=NEUTRAL_GRAY, buff=0)
        bank_label = Text("Bank", font_size=24, color=NEUTRAL_GRAY).next_to(bank_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        bank_group = VGroup(bank_arrow, bank_label)
        self.place_in_area(bank_group, "C3", "D4")
        
        self.play(Create(bank_arrow), Write(bank_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display context words 'River' and 'Water' as blue-colored vectors drifting toward 'Bank'
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)

        river_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.8, color=CONTEXT_BLUE, buff=0)
        river_label = Text("River", font_size=20, color=CONTEXT_BLUE).next_to(river_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        river_group = VGroup(river_arrow, river_label)
        self.place_at_grid(river_group, "B2")

        water_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.8, color=CONTEXT_BLUE, buff=0)
        water_label = Text("Water", font_size=20, color=CONTEXT_BLUE).next_to(water_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        water_group = VGroup(water_arrow, water_label)
        self.place_at_grid(water_group, "E5")

        self.play(FadeIn(river_group), FadeIn(water_group))
        
        # Drifting animation toward the center (Bank)
        self.play(
            river_group.animate.move_to(bank_group.get_center() + LEFT*0.5 + UP*0.5).set_opacity(0.3),
            water_group.animate.move_to(bank_group.get_center() + RIGHT*0.5 + DOWN*0.5).set_opacity(0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate the 'Bank' vector gradually turning blue
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)

        self.play(
            bank_arrow.animate.set_color(CONTEXT_BLUE),
            bank_label.animate.set_color(CONTEXT_BLUE),
            FadeOut(river_group),
            FadeOut(water_group),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Predict the next word: "Flowing"
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)

        prediction_box = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=0.8, color=WHITE)
        prediction_text = Text("Next: Flowing", font_size=24, color=CONTEXT_BLUE)
        prediction_group = VGroup(prediction_box, prediction_text)
        self.place_at_grid(prediction_group, "F4")

        self.play(Create(prediction_box), Write(prediction_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final emphasis
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT)
        
        glow = bank_arrow.copy().set_stroke(width=10).set_color(CONTEXT_BLUE).set_opacity(0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow), bank_group.animate.scale(1.1))
        self.play(FadeOut(glow))
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset colors for end of scene
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

outline.title: The Library Analogy: Query, Key, and Value
outline.content: Introduce the three functional components of the Attention mechanism: Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V). Explain the mechanism as a database search where the 'Query' is what you are looking for, 'Key' is the label on the shelf, and 'Value' is the information inside.
outline.example: A character named 'Detective Query' enters a library. He holds a note (The Word). The library shelves have labels (Keys). He compares his note to every label to see which one matches (Similarity Score). Once matched, he takes the book content (Value) from the shelf.

storyboard.title: The Library Analogy: Query, Key, and Value
lecture_lines: The Query represents the word looking for context.
Keys are labels used to find matches.
Matching labels unlock the word's hidden Value.
Similarity scores determine how much information to take.
This database search forms the core of attention.
animations: Introduce the 'Query' (Q) as a floating magnifying glass icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magn.svg] (#00FFFF) labeled 'What we want'.
Show 'Keys' (K) as labeled folders (#F0E68C) on a shelf, representing the searchable index.
Animate the Query icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magn.svg] moving past the Keys, pausing at each to 'compare' similarity.
Display numerical 'Similarity Scores' above each Key, with one score being significantly higher than others.
Open the folder with the highest score to reveal the 'Value' (V) inside, representing the retrieved information (#ADFF2F).

        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Color constants

        COLOR_K = "#F0E68C"

outline.title: The Math of Focus: Dot Products and Softmax
outline.content: Visualize the mathematical process of calculating 'Attention Scores.' Use the Dot Product to measure the alignment (similarity) between Q and K. Apply the Softmax function to turn these scores into percentages (weights) that sum to 100%.
outline.example: A graphic showing the word 'Eating' (Query) interacting with 'Robot' (Key 1) and 'Pizza' (Key 2). The dot product produces a high score for 'Pizza'. Softmax turns this into: Pizza (90% focus), Robot (10% focus).

storyboard.title: The Math of Focus: Dot Products and Softmax
lecture_lines: Dot products measure alignment between Queries and Keys.
Softmax converts these scores into percentage weights.
Higher weights signal stronger focus on specific words.
The sum of all weights equals 100 percent.
This math directs the model's spotlight precisely.
animations: Display the word 'Eating' as vector Q (#00FFFF) and 'Robot' (K1) and 'Pizza' (K2) as vectors (#FF6347).
Show the Dot Product calculation Q · K1 and Q · K2, with the Pizza result glowing brighter.
Transition the scores into a Softmax layer represented by a bar chart.
Scale the bars to show 'Pizza' at 90% and 'Robot' at 10% focus weights.
Highlight the resulting focus on 'Pizza' with a glowing border (#FFFF00).

import numpy as np

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        dot_apple = Dot(p_apple, color=color_apple)

        label_king = MathTex(r"\text{King}", color=color_king, font_size=20).next_to(dot_king, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_queen = MathTex(r"\text{Queen}", color=color_queen, font_size=20).next_to(dot_queen, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_man = MathTex(r"\text{Man}", color=color_man, font_size=20).next_to(dot_man, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_woman = MathTex(r"\text{Woman}", color=color_woman, font_size=20).next_to(dot_woman, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_apple = MathTex(r"\text{Apple}", color=color_apple, font_size=20).next_to(dot_apple, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        dots = VGroup(dot_king, dot_queen, dot_man, dot_woman, dot_apple)
        labels = VGroup(label_king, label_queen, label_man, label_woman, label_apple)

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[Create(d) for d in dots],
                *[Write(l) for l in labels],
                lag_ratio=0.2
            )
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Clustered positions
        c_king = axes.c2p(1, 2)
        c_man = axes.c2p(1, 1.2)
        c_queen = axes.c2p(1.8, 2)
        c_woman = axes.c2p(1.8, 1.2)
        c_apple = axes.c2p(4.5, 2.5)

        self.play(
            dot_king.animate.move_to(c_king),
            label_king.animate.next_to(c_king, UP, buff=0.1),
            dot_man.animate.move_to(c_man),
            label_man.animate.next_to(c_man, DOWN, buff=0.1),
            dot_queen.animate.move_to(c_queen),
            label_queen.animate.next_to(c_queen, UP, buff=0.1),
            dot_woman.animate.move_to(c_woman),
            label_woman.animate.next_to(c_woman, DOWN, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Vector Equation
        equation = MathTex(
            r"\vec{v}_{\text{King}}", "-", r"\vec{v}_{\text{Man}}", "+", r"\vec{v}_{\text{Woman}}", "=", r"\vec{v}_{\text{Queen}}",
            font_size=28
        )
        equation[0].set_color(color_king)
        equation[2].set_color(color_man)
        equation[4].set_color(color_woman)
        equation[6].set_color(color_queen)

        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(equation))

        # Show the relationship with arrows
        v_man = Arrow(axes.c2p(0,0), dot_man.get_center(), buff=0, color=color_man, stroke_width=2)
        v_king = Arrow(axes.c2p(0,0), dot_king.get_center(), buff=0, color=color_king, stroke_width=2)
        
        v_diff = Arrow(dot_man.get_center(), dot_king.get_center(), buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(v_man), Create(v_king))
        self.play(Create(v_diff))
        
        target_queen_pos = dot_woman.get_center() + (dot_king.get_center() - dot_man.get_center())
        v_result = Arrow(dot_woman.get_center(), target_queen_pos, buff=0, color=color_queen, stroke_width=3)
        
        self.play(
            v_diff.animate.move_to(dot_woman.get_center() + (dot_king.get_center() - dot_man.get_center())/2),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(Create(v_result))
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: Multi-Head Attention: Many Perspectives at Once
outline.content: Explain that Transformers don't just look at a sentence once; they look at it through 'Multi-Head Attention.' Each 'head' focuses on different relationships like grammar, tense, or sentiment simultaneously.
outline.example: An owl with multiple sets of eyes. One set of eyes looks for 'Who did what?' (Subject-Verb), another set looks for 'Where did it happen?' (Location), and a third looks for 'How does it feel?' (Sentiment).

storyboard.title: Multi-Head Attention: Many Perspectives at Once
lecture_lines: Models process sentences through multiple attention heads.
Each head captures unique linguistic relationships.
Together, they build a rich, multi-perspective understanding.
animations: Display a central word sequence 'The robot ate pizza' in white (#FFFFFF).
Show 'Head 1' (#FF00FF) drawing lines between 'robot' and 'ate' to represent grammar (Subject-Verb).
Show 'Head 2' (#00FF00) drawing lines between 'ate' and 'pizza' to represent semantics (Action-Object).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Multi-Head Attention: Many Perspectives at Once"
        lines = [
            "Models process sentences through multiple attention heads.",
            "Each head captures unique linguistic relationships.",
            "Together, they build a rich, multi-perspective understanding."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Models process sentences through multiple attention heads.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Central word sequence "The robot ate pizza" in white (#FFFFFF)
        word_texts = ["The", "robot", "ate", "pizza"]
        words = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=32, color=WHITE) for w in word_texts])
        
        # Positioning words in a row at row C
        self.place_at_grid(words[0], "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(words[1], "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(words[2], "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(words[3], "C5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(words))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Each head captures unique linguistic relationships.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF") # Magenta for Head 1
        )
        
        # "Head 1" label and connections (Subject-Verb)
        head1_label = Text("Head 1: Grammar", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(head1_label, "B3")
        
        # Line between 'robot' (C3) and 'ate' (C4)
        conn1 = CurvedArrow(
            self.grid["C3"] + UP * 0.3, 
            self.grid["C4"] + UP * 0.3, 
            angle=-TAU/8, 
            color="#FF00FF"
        )
        
        self.play(Write(head1_label), Create(conn1))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Together, they build a rich, multi-perspective understanding.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00") # Green for Head 2
        )
        
        # "Head 2" label and connections (Action-Object)
        head2_label = Text("Head 2: Semantics", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(head2_label, "D4")
        
        # Line between 'ate' (C4) and 'pizza' (C5)
        conn2 = CurvedArrow(
            self.grid["C4"] + DOWN * 0.3, 
            self.grid["C5"] + DOWN * 0.3, 
            angle=TAU/8, 
            color="#00FF00"
        )
        
        self.play(Write(head2_label), Create(conn2))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final cleanup highlight
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Context Problem: Why Words Need Neighbors
outline.content: Introduce the core challenge in Natural Language Processing: polysemy and context. Explain that a word's meaning is fluid and depends entirely on the words surrounding it. This section sets the stage for why 'attention' is necessary for computers to understand nuances.
outline.example: Show two sentences: 'The crane flew over the construction site' vs 'The crane lifted the heavy beam.' An animation highlights the word 'crane' and draws lines to 'flew' in the first and 'heavy beam' in the second to show shifting meaning.

storyboard.title: The Context Problem: Why Words Need Neighbors
lecture_lines: Words often have multiple meanings.
Context defines which meaning is correct.
Attention helps models focus on relevant neighbors.
animations: Display the sentence 'The crane flew over the construction site' in light blue (#ADD8E6) at the top.
Display the sentence 'The crane lifted the heavy beam' in light green (#90EE90) below the first.
Highlight the word 'crane' in both sentences by changing their color to yellow (#FFFF00) and drawing arrows to 'flew' in the first and 'heavy beam' in the second.

            "- Softmax converts these scores into percentage weights.",
            "- Higher weights signal stronger focus on specific words.",
            "- The sum of all weights equals 100 percent.",
            "- This math directs the model's spotlight precisely."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Q (Eating, #00FFFF)
        q_label = Text("Q: 'Eating'", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF")

        k2_label = Text("K2: 'Pizza'", font_size=24, color="#FF6347")
        self.place_at_grid(k1_label, "B6") # Issue 28 fix
        self.place_at_grid(k2_label, "D6") # Issue 28 fix

        # Visualizing vectors/connections
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C3"], end=self.grid["B6"], buff=0.4, color=WHITE)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C3"], end=self.grid["D6"], buff=0.4, color=WHITE)

        self.play(FadeIn(q_label), FadeIn(k1_label), FadeIn(k2_label))

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show the Dot Product calculation Q · K1 and Q · K2
        dot1 = MathTex("Q \\cdot K_1 = 0.1", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        dot2 = MathTex("Q \\cdot K_2 = 0.9", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot1, "B6") # Issue 29 fix (overlaps label, but will indicate score)
        self.place_at_grid(dot2, "D6") # Issue 29 fix

        # We fade out labels to show scores
        self.play(
            FadeOut(k1_label), FadeOut(k2_label),
            FadeIn(dot1), FadeIn(dot2)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Pizza result glowing brighter
        self.play(Indicate(dot2, color=YELLOW, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Transition to Softmax bar chart

            FadeOut(dot1), FadeOut(dot2),

        bar_pizza = Rectangle(height=3.6, width=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        # Group and position
        chart_bars = VGroup(bar_robot, bar_pizza).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(chart_bars, "C4", "F5") # Issue 28 fix
        
        # Labels for bars
        label_robot = Text("Robot", font_size=20).next_to(bar_robot, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        label_pizza = Text("Pizza", font_size=20).next_to(bar_pizza, DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # Higher weights signal stronger focus
        self.play(Create(chart_bars), FadeIn(label_robot), FadeIn(label_pizza))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Scale bars to show 90% and 10% focus weights
        weight_robot = Text("10%", font_size=24).next_to(bar_robot, UP, buff=0.1)
        weight_pizza = Text("90%", font_size=24).next_to(bar_pizza, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        sum_check = MathTex("10\\% + 90\\% = 100\\%", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(sum_check, "B4", "B5") # Issue 29 fix

        self.play(FadeIn(weight_robot), FadeIn(weight_pizza))
        self.play(Write(sum_check))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Highlight the resulting focus on 'Pizza' with a glowing border (#FFFF00)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Math of Focus: Dot Products and Softmax", [
            "- Dot products measure alignment between Queries and Keys.",
            "- Softmax converts these scores into percentage weights.",
            "- Higher weights signal stronger focus on specific words.",
            "- The sum of all weights equals 100 percent.",
            "- This math directs the model's spotlight precisely."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Q (Eating, #00FFFF)
        q_label = Text("Q: 'Eating'", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, "C3") # Issue 27 fix
        
        # K1 (Robot, #FF6347) and K2 (Pizza, #FF6347)
        k1_label = Text("K1: 'Robot'", font_size=24, color="#FF6347")
        k2_label = Text("K2: 'Pizza'", font_size=24, color="#FF6347")
        self.place_at_grid(k1_label, "B6") # Issue 28 fix
        self.place_at_grid(k2_label, "D6") # Issue 28 fix

        # Visualizing vectors/connections
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C3"], end=self.grid["B6"], buff=0.4, color=WHITE)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C3"], end=self.grid["D6"], buff=0.4, color=WHITE)

        self.play(FadeIn(q_label), FadeIn(k1_label), FadeIn(k2_label))
        self.play(Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show the Dot Product calculation Q · K1 and Q · K2
        dot1 = MathTex("Q \\cdot K_1 = 0.1", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        dot2 = MathTex("Q \\cdot K_2 = 0.9", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot1, "B6") # Issue 29 fix (overlaps label, but will indicate score)
        self.place_at_grid(dot2, "D6") # Issue 29 fix

        # We fade out labels to show scores
        self.play(
            FadeOut(k1_label), FadeOut(k2_label),
            FadeIn(dot1), FadeIn(dot2)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Pizza result glowing brighter
        self.play(Indicate(dot2, color=YELLOW, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Transition to Softmax bar chart
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrow1), FadeOut(arrow2), 
            FadeOut(dot1), FadeOut(dot2),
            q_label.animate.scale(0.7).move_to(self.grid["A2"])
        )

        # Softmax layer represented by a bar chart
        bar_robot = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#FF6347", stroke_width=2)
        bar_pizza = Rectangle(height=3.6, width=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        # Group and position
        chart_bars = VGroup(bar_robot, bar_pizza).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(chart_bars, "C4", "F5") # Issue 28 fix
        
        # Labels for bars
        label_robot = Text("Robot", font_size=20).next_to(bar_robot, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        label_pizza = Text("Pizza", font_size=20).next_to(bar_pizza, DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # Higher weights signal stronger focus
        self.play(Create(chart_bars), FadeIn(label_robot), FadeIn(label_pizza))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Scale bars to show 90% and 10% focus weights
        weight_robot = Text("10%", font_size=24).next_to(bar_robot, UP, buff=0.1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        title = "The Library Analogy: Query, Key, and Value"
        lines = [
            "The Query represents the word looking for context.",
            "Keys are labels used to find matches.",
            "Matching labels unlock the word's hidden Value.",
            "Similarity scores determine how much information to take.",
            "This database search forms the core of attention."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Color constants
        COLOR_Q = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_K = "#F0E68C"
        COLOR_V = "#ADFF2F"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The Query represents the word looking for context.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_Q))
        
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magn.svg
        query_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magn.svg").set_color(COLOR_Q)
        query_label = Text("What we want", font_size=18, color=COLOR_Q).next_to(query_icon, UP, buff=0.1)
        query_group = VGroup(query_icon, query_label)

        self.place_at_grid(query_group, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(query_group))

        )

        grid_positions = ["D2", "D3", "D4", "D5"]

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_V)
        )

            self.play(flash.animate.scale(3).set_opacity(0), run_time=0.3)

        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Similarity scores determine how much information to take.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        scores_vals = ["0.12", "0.85", "0.02", "0.01"]
        score_labels = VGroup()
        score_positions = ["C2", "C3", "C4", "C5"]
        
        for i in range(4):

            self.place_at_grid(score_txt, score_positions[i])
            score_labels.add(score_txt)
            
        self.play(Write(score_labels))

        self.wait(1)

        # This database search forms the core of attention.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_V)
        )
        
        # Open highest-scoring folder (Keys[1]) to reveal Value
        value_box = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.6, color=COLOR_V, fill_opacity=0.6)
        value_text = Text("Value", font_size=18, color=BLACK).move_to(value_box.get_center())
        value_group = VGroup(value_box, value_text)
        
        # Resolved Issue 26: Positioning at E4, scale 0.8
        self.place_at_grid(value_group, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Animate "opening"
        self.play(
            keys[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_V).scale(1.1),
            FadeIn(value_group, shift=DOWN)
        )
        
        # Connect Query to Value through Key
        connection = Arrow(query_group.get_bottom(), keys[1].get_top(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(connection))
        
        self.wait(2)

            "Mathematical distances reveal relationships between words."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        color_king = "#FFD700"
        color_queen = "#FF69B4"
        color_man = "#1E90FF"

            axis_config={"color": GREY_C},
            tips=True
        )

        apple_group = VGroup(dot_apple, label_apple)
